newsitem.title: USA: Guardian says to acquire SPS Holdings.
newsitem.headline: Guardian says to acquire SPS Holdings.

text.p: Guardian International Inc said Wednesday it agreed to merge with privately-held alarm security firm SPS Holdings Inc.

Under the merger agreement, all SPS outstanding capital stock will be exchanged for Guardian common stock and SPS will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of Guardian, Guardian said, adding it expects to close the deal by the end of July.

The amount of shares to be issued to SPS shareholders will be based upon a valuation formula that takes into account each entity's monthly recurring revenues, senior debt, and working capital, Guardian said.

With SPS's monthly revenues of $240,000, the merged entity will have about $550,000 in monthly recurring revenues, nearly doubling Guardian's revenues, Norris said. He declined to comment on how the merger would affect Guardian's bottom line.
Guardian closed Tuesday at 5/8, its yearly low. It posted a $0.03 per share loss in the first quarter ended March 31.
Guardian was the result of reverse merger transaction in August 1996, under which Everest Securities Corp merged with Guardian, which at the time was a privately-held company.
The merger is subject to board and bank approvals and a fairness opinion on the transaction, the company said.
SPS shareholders will nominate two members to Guardian's board, including Ken Purcell, principal of equity fund Chartwell Capital Investors, which holds an interest in SPS.
